AMENDMENT_1_true_round_robin_selection.problem_with_the_frozen_procedure: the committed selection shuffles the 71 eligible seeds then fills each seed up to cap_per_seed=8 before moving to the next -- at 150 total points this could exhaust after only ~19 seeds, leaving most of the 71 eligible seeds completely untouched. That is breadth-last, not breadth-first.
AMENDMENT_1_true_round_robin_selection.corrected_procedure: true round-robin: shuffle the 71 eligible seeds ONCE (rng_seed=11) to fix an order; then in repeated PASSES over that fixed order, draw exactly ONE new point per seed per pass (each seed's own points shuffled once, drawn in that shuffled order across passes); skip a seed once its own points are exhausted; stop at exactly 150 total. With 71 eligible seeds this reaches full breadth (all 71 touched) within the first ~3 passes.
AMENDMENT_1_true_round_robin_selection.why: every eligible seed contributes before any seed is sampled deeply, so the density increase reflects added STATE DIVERSITY, not a few prolific seeds

AMENDMENT_2_mixture_proportion_control.problem: adding stolen pole-B branch rows at fixed per-row weight 1.0 while leaving every other row's weight and count untouched increases the STOLEN category's total weight-mass in the loss as count grows (50->100->200), confounding 'more examples' with 'the loss now cares more about this regime' (rebalancing).
AMENDMENT_2_mixture_proportion_control.rule_frozen_before_fitting: hold the STOLEN pole-B branch category's TOTAL weight-mass constant across rungs, at the baseline's own mass (50 rows x 1.0 = 50.0). Each stolen pole-B branch row at rung k is weighted 50.0 / n_k: rung_1 (n=50) -> 1.0 each [unchanged], rung_2 (n=100) -> 0.5 each, rung_3 (n=200) -> 0.25 each. Every other row (all plain rows, all pole-A branches, all non-stolen pole-B branches) keeps its ORIGINAL weight and count, unmodified at every rung.
AMENDMENT_2_mixture_proportion_control.what_this_isolates: whether averaging a FIXED total loss-influence over MORE DISTINCT stolen-flag states (better coverage, less per-point noise/overfitting) improves generalisation -- separated from whether the fit simply reallocates attention toward the category.
AMENDMENT_2_mixture_proportion_control.explicitly_not_the_alternative: scaling every other category's data up proportionally, since that would require new collection outside the stolen regime too

AMENDMENT_3_monotonicity_and_meaningful_.rule: the 'absolute density is the dominant problem' reading requires CLEAR, preferably MONOTONIC improvement across 50 -> 100 -> 200 (correct-rate rising at each step, not merely rung_3 > rung_1), by a margin that does not vanish under the seed-level bootstrap CI -- i.e. rung_3's LCB95 must clear rung_1's point estimate, not merely overlap it favourably.
AMENDMENT_3_monotonicity_and_meaningful_.small_or_non_monotonic: labeled INCONCLUSIVE rather than attributed to density, even if the raw point estimates trend upward
AMENDMENT_3_monotonicity_and_meaningful_.given_cuda_nondeterminism: one fit per rung does not eliminate optimisation noise (SPPPO's own production run already demonstrated this); the monotonicity/margin requirement exists specifically to avoid over-reading a single noisy refit
